Reshaping Teeth reshaping, or gum contouring, helps correct uneven tooth length or shape. The dentist scrapes off excess gum tissue during gum contouring to achieve a more aesthetically pleasing gum line. Invisalign is created in the dental office using impressions of the patient’s teeth.    Invisalign works by using a set of aligners that gradually shift your teeth into the desired position. Introduction to Clear Aligner Treatment Invisalign treatment, in particular, is a popular choice among adults and [teens](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Invisalign-For-Teens-p78247.asp "Invisalign For Teens Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX") in Austin who want to address crooked teeth, crowded teeth, and other orthodontic issues while maintaining a natural appearance.    Unlike traditional metal braces that use metal wires and brackets, clear aligners are custom-made to fit snugly over your teeth, gradually shifting them into a straight smile.    Whether you’re [an adult](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Invisalign-for-Adults-p78592.asp "Invisalign for Adults Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX") seeking a more confident smile or a parent exploring options for your teen, Invisalign in Austin provides a modern, effective way to achieve beautifully aligned teeth.   [Image: Young woman smiling and holding up an Invisalign clear aligner from Sola Smile Co. in Austin, TX.]Benefits of Invisalign Getting Invisalign has [several benefits.](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Benefits-of-Invisalign-p75465.asp "Benefits of Invisalign Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX") The main advantage is that they improve the appearance of your teeth, giving you a dazzling, brighter smile. You may remove clear aligners anytime you want to brush your teeth, eat, or drink because they are removable.   Brushing is an important part of maintaining oral hygiene during Invisalign treatment, as aligners can be taken out to allow thorough brushing and flossing.    Clear aligners are also more aesthetically pleasing since their color precisely mimics your natural teeth. They also require fewer orthodontic appointments and upkeep than conventional braces.   Who Qualifies for Invisalign Treatment? Anyone looking to improve their smile and align their teeth should think about using Invisalign. [Image: Dentist conducting Invisalign consultation at Sola Smile Co. in Austin, TX.]The Invisalign Process Your Austin dentists will inquire about your dental history before starting the Invisalign process. Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX")    Additionally, they will carefully examine your mouth, teeth, and face while taking pictures from various points of view. The next step the dentist will carry out is an interproximal reduction, which comprises widening the spaces between your teeth.    This technique should only be used on people who have crowded teeth. | Dental Technology in South Austin, TX  [Image: Dentist and patient meeting to discuss her oral surgery at Sola Smile Co. in Austin, TX]Diagnosing oral health issues requires a thorough [dental examination](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Dental-Exam-p62281.asp "Dental Exam Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX") of your mouth. We need to look at the structures inside your mouth as well as your face as a whole.    There are certain areas of your mouth, however, that are more difficult to see than others.    Through various dental technologies we have here at our Sola Smile Co. office, we are able to take a closer look at your teeth and gums.   CAD-CAM CAD-CAM, or Computer-Aided Design-Computer Aided Manufacturing, encompasses any kind of software that allows us to perform a wide variety of procedures quicker, more easily, and precisely.    This technology is used in a wide variety of [dental reconstruction](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Full-Mouth-Reconstruction-p81431.asp "Full Mouth Reconstruction Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX") procedures, such as inlays and onlays, bridges, [same day dental crowns](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Same-Day-Crowns-p67154.asp "Same Day Crowns Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX"), and veneers. This technology allows for more affordable pricing for many kinds of procedures, due to the ability to handle more of the reconstructive process in-house.    It also cuts out the need for temporary restorations, which save patients time, while also being more economical.   Cone Beam CT Scan With cone-beam CT, a single round of scanning generates views captured from a wide variety of angles that can be combined to construct highly detailed images of various aspects of a dentition.    Unlike traditional x-rays and CT scans, cone-beam CT scanners can capture both internal and external components of a dentition like the soft tissues and jaw simultaneously.   We may use cone-beam CT scans to evaluate tissue structures in complex cases that require the accurate positioning of implants, [wisdom teeth removal](/p/dentist-South-Austin-TX-Wisdom-Teeth-Removal-p80350.asp "Wisdom Teeth Removal Sola Smile Co. - Dr. Audrey Su Austin, TX dentist South Austin TX"), reconstructive surgery, root canal treatment, evaluation of sinuses, treatments for temporomandibular joint disorder (TMJ), and the investigation of sources of pain in oral pathology.   Intraoral Scanners Intraoral scanners are typically small, handheld devices that are easy for dental professionals to manipulate inside the patient's mouth.    These scanners provide real-time, high-definition 3D imaging, allowing dental practitioners to visualize the scanned area immediately on a computer screen. Intraoral scanning is non-invasive and eliminates the need for traditional dental impressions.   Digital X-Rays When it comes to the details of digital radiography and how it works, there are two basic types: direct and indirect. Direct digital radiography works by having the patient insert a photosensitive imaging device in their mouth to perform a scan.    This device is then loaded into a processor and converted to a digital image.    Indirect digital radiography is the option which offers real-time images of the mouth by bypassing the need for a scanner or processor and converting them directly to a computer. Each method has its own advantages and disadvantages.   Curious About What Else We've Got?
